scope: Re-verification after the security fixes of 2026-10-21/22. The 2026-10-09 models were first run unchanged against the current code (baseline), then brought up to date with the implementation they copy (M1/M1c, M2/M2c, M3, M4, M4s, M5v, M8a, M8k) and extended with M3s, M2x, M4L and M4p. Implementation code is unchanged.

baseline.description: formal-model at 619f934 (the 2026-10-09 models) run against the code at 619f934

service_conformance.title: The real hierarchy guard rejects loss for a superior and accepts loss for a lower member
Removing a superior from an existing private channel is refused
Changing privacy preserves the owner and superior access claimed by H2/H3
Moving categories preserves superior access claimed by H2
Channel/category deletion cannot remove superior permissions; owner operations still succeed
Service mask validators reject integers with bits above the 32-bit model domain
Only a group member orders a commit; a device outside the group replaces it only by confirmed fresh start, and only when no usable member is left (M3 KL-orphan, §5.3.4)
Channel and category HTTP routes return 403 for superior-access loss and accept harmless edits
A sequential unchanged save does not permit a clearing request
An in-flight unchanged save cannot bypass the change-after-warning requirement A3
Concurrent avatar save must recheck the locked current picture
Concurrent avatar remove must recheck the locked current picture
Concurrent requests in two workspaces still consume only one account allowance
Equal decoded pixels give equal sanitized bytes, as the sanitizer contract claims
Re-encoding the unchanged picture cannot enable a clearing request
Existing noncanonical PNGs compare by pixels; actual picture edits remain possible
A committed upload remains readable after the caller receives a transaction error
A request naming a workspace or member in capital letters is refused, so no change escapes the audit view (M5v AV-case)
Who publishes packages in a private channel is shown only to audit viewers who can see the channel (M5v AV-class)
The audit view returns no chain hashes that would show rows written in between (M5v AV-links)
A confirmation taken before its session was revoked no longer lets that session change the password or sign out the others (M4s AS1, AS2)
A socket whose session is revoked while it connects is closed (M4s WS1)
A stolen session that uses up its confirmations cannot keep the owner's other session from confirming and revoking it
At the device limit a registration retires the oldest device nobody approved, ends its sessions and leaves approved devices alone; the operator reset retires every such device (M4 LK1, ES1)
Deleting a passkey ends the other sessions opened with it, keeps the asking session and the sessions opened otherwise, and the last passkey cannot be deleted (M4s PK1)
The same commit sent again gets the replay answer, whichever check finds its version taken (M3r K2)
An upload compared with a current picture that cannot be read does not count as a change; a missing one does (M6 A3)
Concurrent readiness/full verification and appends never report a false rollback
A head write failure preserves the committed result, blocks subsequent writes, and recovers on restart
An unchanged durable audit chain verifies after a real process restart
Startup refuses a missing durable head without silently provisioning it
The explicit head initializer upgrades an authenticated v1 checkpoint without losing its anchor
An invalid persistent head signature is rejected after restart
Startup repairs a lagging head only forward on a verified database chain
Replaying an old checkpoint is rejected by the running implementation
Replaying an old checkpoint and truncated chain is rejected after restart

findings.summary: mls_groups.remove_required_at is kept from the first loss of access while any member who lost access remains (coalesce); after that user regains access, a newer loss is counted from the older one and a manager outside the group can fresh start under rule (c) before anything waited 15 minutes. Confidentiality is unaffected. Not fixed: the fix needs a design decision (per-member loss time, or resetting the time when access returns).
findings.status: fixed the same day: per-member access_lost_at (migration 0026); see addendum_r057

limitations: PASS holds within each model's bounded states and transitions only.

M8k: B's scheduled installs cover every key at B when C joins, and C's keys at B when C joins and leaves (scheduling every key at B there passed 500,000 states by depth 16 and kept growing, so that search was stopped); the insider forges only once the call has settled.
M2x: the manager M acts at depth 3 (its role edits are covered by the main run); the administrator only assigns and removes roles and members.
M3s: X (the manager) keeps the channel; up to 4 versions, 4 access changes, 1 device change, no unreadable envelope.
M4L scales the device limit down from 8 to 3.

addendum_r057.summary: R-057 fixed: each current member keeps mls_group_members.access_lost_at (set when its user loses the channel, kept while the user stays without it, cleared when the user sees it again); pendingSince counts each removal from its own member (a revoked device from its revocation). Migration 0026 drops mls_groups.remove_required_at and gives the current members of groups that had it the migration time, which can only delay rule (c).
